chunks: But the unbelievers would like to stare you out of balance when they hear the warning, and say: 'Surely he is possessed;'

key_terms.يَكَادُ: to be on the verge of / almost
key_terms.يُزْلِقُونَكَ: they would make you slip / stagger you

ai.seo_question: What did the disbelievers say about the Prophet when they heard the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the psychological intensity of the Meccan opposition, where the 'gaze' (abṣār) is interpreted not merely as staring but as a weapon of spiritual pressure and envy against the Prophet's divine authority. The accusation of madness (majnūn) reflects their inability to comprehend the profound impact of the Quranic discourse on their hearts, a theme often linked to the concept of 'Ismah (infallibility) protecting the Prophet from their subtle attacks.
